footer.sample: Accounts, cards and amounts on these screens are examples, not real data

home.lead: A credit line shared across cards, billing that closes on business days with Chilean holidays, installments that commit the credit line on purchase day, carry-over of what you couldn't pay. What other apps simplify until the numbers stop adding up.
home.sub: No bank connections and no automatic sync: nothing enters your account that you didn't record. Pesos, dollars and UF, with no made-up conversions.

accountTypes.title: Different account types
accountTypes.body: Checking, sight, savings, credit card, prepaid and cash. Each one behaves like it does at your bank.

businessDays.title: Business days, your way
businessDays.body: You choose how many business days until the closing date and how many until payment. Chilean holidays are already counted.

currencies.title: Pesos, dollars and UF
currencies.body: Each account in its own currency with its own total. No conversions your bank wouldn't recognize.

noBanks.title: No connected banks
noBanks.body: Nothing comes in unless you record it. You sign in with your RUT and close your sessions whenever you want.

product.title: The product
product.subtitle: The app's real screens, with sample data. Each view comes with the rules that govern it.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.subtitle: Where the money lives, and where the debt lives. They're not the same.
accounts.p1: An account is where there's a balance or a credit line. Your credit card is its own account, not a channel over your checking account: the bank sells them together, but a purchase doesn't take money out — it opens revolving debt with its own statement, cycle and minimum payment.
accounts.p2: Only the last four digits of each card are stored. The full number never leaves your browser and the CVV is never asked for. An account's first credit card inherits its credit line; the next ones choose between sharing it or having their own limit per currency.
accounts.p3: The cash account is created with your user and the last one can't be deleted: the bills in your wallet exist whether the app models them or not.

pools.title: Account credit lines
pools.sharedHint: Primary and additional cards both draw from here
pools.additionalHint: Another currency: independent pool, no conversion

cards.cashNote: Created with your user and can't be deleted

accounts.footnote: Each tile leads to the account, where its cards, billing and movements live. A credit card shows debt instead of a balance, in an attention color and with its credit used at the bottom.

billing.title: Billing
billing.p1: It isn't a separate menu section: it lives inside the account, next to its movements. The open period accumulates and its total is the live sum of its movements, so you fix one and the total fixes itself. It closes 20 business days after the previous cut-off, and from there 10 business days run until the due date.
billing.p2: Any payment settles the period. What you didn't cover moves to the next one as a previous balance, with a record of where it went, and the credit line frees up only by what you actually paid: the rest is still debt.
billing.note: No made-up interest figure: the model has no such concept. An issuer charge is recorded as a finance charge and counts toward the total like any other.

movements.title: Movements
movements.subtitle: 7 movements · August 2026
movements.p1: Expense, income or a transfer between your own accounts. Each movement is checked against your credit line, your declared overdraft and the balance ceiling of a sight account: nothing your bank would reject gets in as if it had happened.
movements.p2: A credit card expense doesn't lower your account balance: it raises credit used, and the money leaves only once, when you pay the statement.
movements.p3: A transfer is two rows joined by a group — an expense at the source, income at the destination — so each account sees its own side. They're left out of category totals so they don't inflate your monthly spending.

financeCharge.title: Finance charge
financeCharge.body: An issuer charge — revolving interest, a fee, insurance — isn't made by any card. The app never calculates it: you read it from your statement and record it. That's what lets the carried-over balance match your real statement.

movements.footnote: The {{transfer}} transfer shows up as a row in each account, but doesn't count toward the {{expenses}} of monthly expenses: moving money between your accounts isn't spending.

credit.title: With a credit card
credit.body: The whole credit line is committed on purchase day, like your issuer does, but billing only charges the installment that's due. The purchase is excluded from the period total so it isn't charged twice. An installment goes from scheduled to billed to paid through the period's closing and payment, never by hand.

noCredit.title: Without a credit card
noCredit.body: Each installment is a real expense from the account you choose. If you pay less, the shortfall moves to the next installment without rewriting the schedule.

delete.title: Deleting a plan
delete.body: Reverts its whole history: removes its expenses, returns the balance to each account and frees the credit line. The confirmation tells you how much it will move before doing it.

debts.title: Debts
debts.subtitle: 2 active debts · 2 people
debts.intro: Marking one paid moves real money — it creates the movement and adjusts the account balance. Undoing it reverts it by the same amount, because exactly what it moved is recorded.

real.title: Paying moves real money
real.body: Marking a debt as paid creates the movement and adjusts the account balance. You don't type the amount: it comes from the debt's own schedule.

undo.title: And undoing it gives it back
undo.body: Exactly what each payment moved is recorded, so reverting it deletes that movement and restores the balance by the same amount.

noDebt.title: No paying debt with debt
noDebt.body: You can't settle a debt from a credit card account, and the account must be in the same currency: there's no conversion.

recurring.title: Recurring
recurring.subtitle: 2 active · 1 paused
recurring.intro: Subscriptions, rent, insurance. The next date is calculated from the series' anchor, and you can pause one without losing its history.

reminder.title: A reminder, not a charge
reminder.body: A series doesn't create movements on its own: it tells you what's coming and when, and you record the expense when it really happens.

frequency.title: Weekly, monthly or yearly
frequency.body: With its own interval — every two weeks, every three months — and the next date calculated from the series' anchor.

pause.title: Pause without losing history
pause.body: A paused series stops showing up in what's coming, but it's still there to resume when you subscribe again.

savings.title: Savings
savings.subtitle: 3 goals · 2 in progress, 1 complete
savings.paceSummary: Pace over the last 3 months: {{amount}} per month
savings.intro: Progress and pace always derive from your real contributions — each one is an expense in the source account, so they can't be inflated.

real.title: Contributing is a real expense
real.body: Each contribution comes out of one of your accounts and is recorded as a movement, so progress can't be inflated by typing a number.

pace.title: Your contributions set the pace
pace.body: It's the average of the last three full calendar months, not a target you set when you created the goal.

close.title: Closing has three destinations
close.body: Withdraw to an account, move to free savings or transfer to another goal. Withdrawing is reversible: reopening undoes the movement it created.

about.title: Why FinanceApp exists
about.p1: Almost every personal finance app treats the credit card as just another account: the purchase lowers your balance, all twelve installments land in the same month, the closing date falls on the same day of the month for everyone and “available” adds pesos to dollars. None of that is true, and one month is enough for your numbers to stop matching the bank's.
about.p2: FinanceApp is built the other way around: first the rules of the real product — shared credit line, closing on business days, billed installment, carry-over of the unpaid balance — and then the screen. If the model can't honestly back a figure, the app doesn't show it.
about.principlesTitle: How we decide what goes in

reviewable.title: Nothing automatic you can't review
reviewable.body: There's no bank sync. You record things, which is why the data is yours and you know where it came from.

noInvented.title: No made-up figures
noInvented.body: The app doesn't calculate your bank's interest or convert currencies. When a piece of data is missing, it says so instead of filling it with an estimate.

reversible.title: Everything reversible
reversible.body: Undoing a debt payment returns the balance. Deleting an installment plan reverts its whole history, and tells you how much it will move before doing it.

chileFirst.title: Chile first, done right
chileFirst.body: Legal holidays, RUT with check digit, UF, banks and credit unions from the local catalogue. One country done fully rather than many done halfway.

about.todayBody: It works with accounts, cards, movements, billing, installments, goals, debts and recurring expenses, in pesos, dollars and UF. What doesn't exist yet isn't dressed up as a feature: investment tracking is on hold and exporting your data isn't ready yet.

privacy.title: Privacy & data
privacy.subtitle: What's stored, who gets in and how you leave
privacy.p1: Your balances, movements and debts describe your financial situation, so they're treated as sensitive data: permission to process them is asked for separately, explicitly and versioned, never hidden inside an “I accept the terms”. Your consent history can be reviewed in your profile.
privacy.p2: You sign in with your RUT, just like your bank — email is only for notices. If your device supports it, with a passkey instead of a password.

sessions.title: Sessions & devices
sessions.subtitle: Close one and its access dies on the very next request, not at the next refresh.
sessions.note: A closed session is kept for 3 days so you can see it, then deleted. Approximate geolocation by IP.

passkey.title: Passkey
passkey.body: Skips password and second factor, because it's already strong authentication on its own.

mfa.title: Second factor
mfa.body: TOTP with recovery codes. Changing it closes every other session, in the same transaction.

deletion.title: Deleting your account
deletion.body: Full erasure, or anonymization if you'd rather keep the history with nothing that identifies you.

minors.title: Minors
minors.body: Sign-up with authorization from a mother, father or guardian, stored as a separate consent.

banks.title: We don't connect to your bank
banks.body: There's no automatic sync and no read access to your products. Nothing comes in unless you record it.

cardNumber.title: We don't store your card number
cardNumber.body: Only the last four digits. The full number never leaves your browser and the CVV is never asked for.

estimates.title: We don't calculate or estimate for you
estimates.body: No interest, no exchange rate, no “projected” expenses you haven't recorded.

attachments.title: Your receipts
attachments.body: They're validated by their real content, not the file extension, and opened through a signed link that expires in five minutes. The name they're stored under doesn't reveal who you are or which movement they belong to.

hideBalances.title: Hide balances
hideBalances.body: A switch in your profile masks the app's amounts, and you can reveal a single one when you need it. Handy for checking your accounts around other people.

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.subtitle: One answer, no comparison table
pricing.freeHint: No tiers, no artificial limits and no locked features.

included.accounts: Every account and card you have
included.movements: Movements, transfers and receipts with no cap
included.billing: Billing, installments, goals, debts and recurring
included.security: Passkey, second factor and session control

whyFree.title: Why it doesn't cost anything
whyFree.body: The expensive part of a finance app is connecting to banks: an intermediary is paid for every synced account, and that cost is charged to you or paid with your data. There's no such connection here, so there's no such cost.

notYourData.title: Your data isn't the price
notYourData.body: No ads, no profiling for third parties and your movements aren't sold. Free here means free, not “paid some other way”.

changes.title: If something changes, we'll tell you first
changes.body: If some part ever has a real cost — storing lots of receipts, for example — you'll be told before it happens, with the option to take your data with you. Nothing becomes paid overnight.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.subtitle: The questions that come up in the first month, grouped by topic. If something isn't here, the answer is almost always the same: the app doesn't show a figure it can't back.

bankSync.q: Does it connect to my bank?
bankSync.a: No. You record your accounts and movements. It's more work on day one and, in exchange, no app has read access to your products.

setup.q: Do I have to set everything up before using it?
setup.a: No. Your cash account is created with you, at zero, so you can log an expense on day one and add your accounts and cards when you have time.

conversion.q: Does it convert between pesos, dollars and UF?
conversion.a: No. Each account lives in its own currency and each total is shown separately, so you never get a sum your bank wouldn't recognize.

investments.q: Does it work for my investments?
investments.a: You can have an investment account and record its movements, but tracking instruments and returns doesn't exist yet. We'd rather say so than show you an empty screen.

creditBalance.q: Why didn't my credit card purchase lower my balance?
creditBalance.a: Because it shouldn't. A credit purchase raises your credit used, it doesn't lower your balance: the money leaves only once, later, when you pay the statement.

closing.a: When you say: you set how many business days pass since the previous cut-off, or a fixed day of the month if your issuer works that way. Chilean holidays are already counted, and the payment date is configured separately.

partialPayment.q: What happens if I pay less than the total?
partialPayment.a: The period is settled and what you didn't cover moves to the next one as a previous balance, with a record of where it went. Your credit line frees up only by what you actually paid.

additionalCard.q: Does the additional card spend from my same credit line?
additionalCard.a: Yes, just like at your bank — unless you give it its own limit, which is still capped by the account's credit line. Each card also shows how much it spent.

interest.q: Does it calculate the interest I'm charged?
interest.a: No, and on purpose: making up a rate would make your numbers stop matching your statement. You record it as a finance charge and it's added where it belongs.

signIn.a: With your RUT and password, or with a passkey if your device supports it. Email is only for notices.

deleteAccount.q: Can I really delete my account?
deleteAccount.a: Yes. You can erase everything, or keep the history with no data that identifies you. Either way your sessions and passkeys are deleted.

minors.q: I'm a minor, can I use it?
minors.a: Yes, with authorization from your mother, father or guardian. The sign-up form asks for it on its own. Their RUT is stored only as a hash, because they're a third party and not an app user.

cta.body: Creating the account takes a minute and commits you to nothing: you can log your first expense in cash.
